property_summary: The owner() function must return the address that was set as the owner during construction via Ownable._transferOwnership, not address(0); the bug returns address(0) for any non-zero owner, violating this invariant.
The return value of owner() must equal the address passed as _owner during construction/transfer, but the buggy version returns msg.sender instead, which breaks immutability of ownership.
After a successful transferOwnership call, the owner() of the reference contract equals the newOwner parameter, whereas the buggy mutant always sets owner() to address(0).
Transferring ownership to the zero address is always disallowed in the reference, but allowed in the buggy version.
The owner() address must never change to the zero address after any call to transferOwnership, but the buggy version allows it.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner must not be address(0); the buggy version allows transferring ownership to address(0), violating this invariant.
After a call to transferOwnership(address(0)), the state variable owner remains unchanged in the reference but changes to address(0) in the buggy version.

After any transferOwnership call, the previous owner must not be able to renounce ownership again; the buggy version with zero-address allowed breaks by changing owner to zero, allowing subsequent re-renounce.
Only the current owner can successfully call transferOwnership; the bug allows any caller to transfer ownership without being owner.
setRewardDistributor must update the rewardDistributor state variable to the new address
The setRewardDistributor function must actually update the rewardDistributor state variable.
After calling setRewardDistributor, the rewardDistributor is always set to the argument passed.
Only the owner can successfully change the reward distributor.
